text:
Alex: putting together an appendix for SOC2 retention mapping — want a small data-classification table + short SDK redaction example for audit logs. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432 (WIP). Which classification buckets should we show?
Mira: agree on table. I'd include: Audit Logs, Operational Metrics, Customer Content, System Metadata. Columns: classification | retention_days | example_item | storage | redaction_applied
Mira: sample table:
```
classification | retention_days | example_item | storage | redaction_applied
Audit Logs | 365 | auth.login, api.request | encrypted-s3 | partial (ip hashed)
Operational Metrics | 90 | cpu, latency | metrics-db | none
Customer Content | variable | customer.chat, uploads | customer-sandbox | redacted by policy
System Metadata | 30 | server_id, build_id | internal-logs | none
```
Kevin: for SDK snippet, we should show both export and redaction flag. small python example:
```
# python SDK snippet
from redwood import AuditClient
c = AuditClient()
export = c.export_logs(filter="service:auth", redact=True, retention_days=365)
print(export.url)
```
Mira: also add curl example for audit export + redaction param:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"filter":"service:auth","redact":true,"format":"ndjson"}'
```
Sam: small legal note — avoid using 'PII' as a tech classification. prefer 'customer_personal_data' and call out consent requirement. i'll ping legal for wording: @Rachel-legal
Mira: got it, will swap terminology. also will add one-liner on how redaction works and a link to the SDK redaction docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/redaction
docs-bot: PR opened by mira: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432 — CI checks started :github:
Alex: perfect. next steps: Mira to update table + examples, Kevin to add python snippet and unit-tested example export, Sam to get legal ok. target merge by EOD Thu. :white_check_mark:
